correctness.rationale: Explicit monomial integration gives exact diagonal and one q-spaced off-diagonal of H_g. Rational expansion yields d_k=-2Q/k^3+6P/k^4+O(k^-5) and the offdiagonal k^-4 coefficient; a gauge and exact quadratic-form identity lead to V_k=2(B-Q)/k^3+W/k^4+O(k^-5). The factorization Q-B=m^3|b|^2(r-n/m)(r-(n/m)^2), plus exact W signs +4n^2(n-m)^2|b|^2 at the lower edge and -2n^3(n-m)^2|b|^2/m at the upper, determines every boundary. Remote tent blocks and negative isolated coordinate tests prove respective infinite min–max inertia; negative potential tails give finite positive inertia. Hilbert–Schmidt T_g proves H_g trace class and trace zero, and band truncation plus negative coordinate min–max give s_j(H_g) comparable to j^-3. The actual packaged standalone verifier replays 5,485 finite matrix/rational/asymptotic/boundary checks. Infinite claims use analytical estimates, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Spectral inertia and the ideal exponent are natural, independent diagnostics of nonnormality of polynomial-symbol integration operators on Bergman space. The full ratio phase transition between finite and infinite positive index, and opposite inclusion at the two naturally occurring roots, are nontrivial fourth-order structural information not implied by the classical T_g Schatten criterion. The theorem works uniformly for arbitrary integer exponents and complex coefficients, not for an arbitrary isolated finite sample, and identifies the sharp Schatten boundary for the commutator.
